title: Quantum resources in non-stoquastic quantum annealing
summary: Quantum annealing promises to solve combinatorial optimization problems by preparing the ground state of a target Hamiltonian. Standard annealing protocols are, however, stoquastic and can thus be simulated by sign-problem-free quantum Monte-Carlo methods. To obtain a true quantum advantage, it has been proposed to use non-stoquastic catalyst Hamiltonians. Active only at intermediate stages of the protocol, these can, for certain problems, convert first-order into second-order quantum phase transitions and thus permit an exponential speedup over the stoquastic protocol.
